Alex (PM): Quick sync — let's map Q3/Q4 roadmap for Private deployments. Top asks from customers: VPC control plane parity, on‑prem packaging, and air‑gapped install. Need concrete launch criteria and tradeoffs.
Jordan (Eng): +1. We need to pick MVP boundaries. My proposal: MVP = VPC control plane (cloud control plane + tenant VPC networking), on‑prem dmg/tarball for evaluation, air‑gapped as follow‑on.
Carla (Sales): Customers pushing for air‑gapped from day 1 (HealthCo, FinBank). They're ok with phased rollout if we lock SLA/upgrade story.
Sam (SRE): Operational checklist: automated backups, upgrade rollback, health probes, metrics export (Prom), and runbook. Can't commit to SLA until we prove install reliability in 3 pilot sites.
Teri (Security): Must include KMS/HSM integration, signed packages, integrity checks, and an audit log export path. Air‑gapped installs require offline KMS key bootstrap doc.
Maria (Research): Performance note: control plane routing needs to preserve token-level latency — design should allow routing to local inference vs hosted fallback without affecting session state.
Alex (PM): Launch criteria idea: 1) Packaging + installer that completes in <2 hrs for a standard 4‑node cluster; 2) Security checklist satisfied (KMS + signatures); 3) E2E upgrade test w/ rollback; 4) 3 pilot customers onboarded. Thoughts?
Jordan (Eng): Feasible if we scope installer to containerized distro + documented manual steps. Full operator (helm + CRDs) would be v2. For air‑gapped, we can produce an image bundle + offline registry tarball.
Sam (SRE): Agree. Also need an acceptance test harness that runs post‑install: `curl /health`, KV cache sanity, latency smoke test. We should keep these tests as part of the package.
Teri (Security): For signed packages: recommend using cosign and provide sample key rotation procedure. For air‑gapped, include detached signatures and checksums alongside the tarball.
Carla (Sales): Timeline sensitivity: two customers want pilot in 6–8 weeks. If we accept that, we must deprioritize automation and focus on a deterministic manual installer + runbook.
Jordan (Eng): Can do a manual installer + packaged images for pilots. Engineering estimate: 4 weeks to make VPC control plane deployable (cloud side + onboarding flow), 3 weeks to assemble image bundle + installer script, 2 weeks for basic tests. Total ~9 weeks for pilot.
Alex (PM): OKR alignment: Private GA target Q4. Proposed OKR: "Ship Private Pilot and secure 3 paid pilots" (KR: pilot onboarding docs, signed package, KMS integration, runbook + 3 pilots).
Maria (Research): We should add a quality KR: regression suite against prompt sets to detect model-serving differences in private vs hosted. Small token sample must be identical within tolerance.
Sam (SRE): Operational KR: automated backup and restore validated in staging. Also SLA gating: we set internal readiness threshold — only after 3 successful restores do we approve SLA comms.
Teri (Security): Add compliance KR: run security checklist with one customer and produce an attestation doc.
Alex (PM): Decisions to make now: A) MVP scope = VPC control plane + manual on‑prem installer (pilot) vs full operator; B) Air‑gapped = pilot severity (do we commit to pilot air‑gapped deliverable); C) SLA commitment timeline. Vote?
Jordan (Eng): Vote A: manual installer MVP. B: yes, provide air‑gapped pilot bundle. C: SLA only post‑pilot validation.
Sam (SRE): +1 to Jordan.
Teri (Security): +1 but security signoff required before pilot.
Carla (Sales): +1, customers accept pilot with clear known limitations documented.
Alex (PM): Good — action items: 1) Jordan: produce installer prototype + image bundle (owner) — due in 3 weeks; 2) Sam: test harness + runbook templates — due in 3 weeks; 3) Teri: package signing + KMS bootstrap doc — due in 2 weeks; 4) Carla: pick 2 pilot customers and scope success criteria — due EOD Friday.
Jordan (Eng): I'll open the repo `private-deliverables/installer-prototype` and add checklist.
deploy-bot: CI passed — branch: installer-prototype (unit tests: 12/12).
Alex (PM): We'll hold a check-in next Tue to review artifacts. If a blocker surfaces, escalate to eng leadership. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
